newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND, FRANCE SET FOR FIVE NATIONS CRUNCH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND, FRANCE SET FOR FIVE NATIONS CRUNCH.

text.p: France have two weeks to locate a flaw in England's sweetly-tuned Five Nations chariot if they want to keep their own high-scoring grand slam challenge intact at Twickenham on March 1.

England's record 46-6 thrashing of Ireland in Dublin and France's thrilling 27-22 victory over Wales at Parc des Princes have ensured another instalment of "le crunch" which so often settles the tournament.
The English have not lost at Twickenham to their cross-Channel rivals for a decade, and the biggest worry for Gallic supporters is the sight of them losing their try-scoring inhibitions.

Six tries at Lansdowne Road, including two apiece for wingers Jon Sleightholme and Tony Underwood, boosted England's tally to 10 in just two Five Nations games this season, a startling improvement on their pre-Christmas strike-rate against Argentina and the New Zealand Barbarians.

As in their 41-13 romp against Scotland, they saved the best until last with five tries in the final 15 minutes, a further illustration of how much pressure their big pack is exerting in the opening hour.

When they develop the confidence to attempt their dazzling broken-field rugby earlier, they could be even more threatening and coach Jack Rowell, whose critics have now ducked out of sight, is not yet satisfied.

"Some of the things we spoke of during the week like keeping our shape and keeping control of the ball we didn't always do," Rowell said. "But we are getting better as a team and we can improve further."

His opposite number Brian Ashton felt Ireland had been "naive" but they were scarcely helped by the loss of fly-half Eric Elwood and number eight Eric Miller through injury inside the first 26 minutes
The sobering truth, as replacements Austin Healey and Jeremy Guscott showed, is that England have a pool of talent which Ireland can only dream about.
The consolation for France, who beat the Irish 32-15 last month, is that they also have back-up players more than capable of shining in an international jersey.

They look certain to be without centre Richard Dourthe for the rest of the championship after he dislocated a shoulder against Wales, and several normally key players will still be unavailable for Twickenham.

But such misfortune has served only to unveil fresh talents like David Venditti, who has four tries in two Five Nations games, Christophe Lamaison and Laurent Leflamand, whose two tries finally edged out the Welsh.

His second, France's fourth, owed much to one of the season's cruellest bounces but French coach Jean-Claude Skrela was grateful for any assistance in the absence of half his probable first-choice side.
"Everything was not perfect. We dropped too many balls and physically, we suffered," he admitted. "But the players really tried to play exciting rugby and that's satisfying."

Assistant coach Pierre Villepreux acknowledged: "The Welsh have improved a lot since the players who had switched codes came back. They now have powerful players capable of keeping the ball. They may soon become a very difficult team to beat."

Welsh skipper Jonathan Humphreys, whose side have already scored 10 Five Nations tries, their best return for 17 years, was left to contemplate his side's second successive defeat by five points or fewer.

"We came here believing we were going to win and we're very disappointed to fall a few points short again. How many times have a Welsh side come to Parc des Princes, scored three tries and finished on the losing side?"
"At least we've got England in Cardiff in a month's time. I'm sure all of Wales will look forward to that and I'm sure England won't."
Coach Kevin Bowring agreed. "We're improving and we're moving in the right direction," he said. "We're certainly not afraid of England."
